inputs.name: kestra_version
inputs.description: Tag of the Kestra image, such as "v2.0.9-slim", Kestra with its core tasks only, or "v2.0.9", with every plugin. Change image_digest with it.

inputs.name: image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of the image for kestra_version, such as "sha256:3ee7...". Podman pulls by the digest, so a tag that moves upstream can't change what runs.

inputs.name: image_repository
inputs.description: Where to pull Kestra's image from, such as a mirror of docker.io/kestra/kestra.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Host address Kestra's web server is published on. The default keeps it on the host for a reverse proxy in front; "0.0.0.0" publishes it on every address.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: Host port Kestra's web server is published on.

inputs.name: public_url
inputs.description: The address people reach Kestra at, such as "https://kestra.example.com". Kestra uses it for links in notifications and webhook URLs. When null, the local address from listen_address and port.

inputs.name: admin
inputs.description: The account to sign in with, such as { email = "you@example.com" }. Kestra's open-source edition has one. When null, Kestra shows a setup page to whoever opens it first.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password for admin. Needed with admin. Kestra wants 8 to 256 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_admin_password; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: postgres
inputs.description: PostgreSQL to keep Kestra's flows, executions and queue in, such as { host = "db1.lan" }. The role and database must exist. When null, Kestra uses an H2 database in /var/lib/kestra/db.

inputs.name: postgres_password
inputs.description: Password of the postgres username. Needed with postgres. Pass it at run time; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: secrets
inputs.description: Secrets your flows read with secret("NAME"), such as { GITHUB_TOKEN = "..." }. The circuit base64-encodes each one into SECRET_NAME, the form Kestra reads, in a root-only env file. They never reach the plan or state.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: More environment variables for Kestra, such as { KESTRA_TASKS_TMPDIR_PATH = "/app/storage/tmp" }. Kestra reads any of its settings from a variable named after it. They go in the root-only env file and never reach the plan or state.
